title: 350 nm QW-Centered 36-Layer DBR with Bounded Perturbation
scientific_hypothesis: Shifting the quarter-wave initialization center from 360 nm to 350 nm will improve spectral anchoring in the UV transition zone (355-365 nm stopband edge), reducing passband ripple while maintaining dual-stopband suppression. Bounded ±15 nm perturbation for early iterations will smooth late-layer thickness oscillations observed in prior runs.
design_principle: Modified quarter-wavelength optimization with shifted reference wavelength and staged perturbation bounds per feedback directive.
proposed_topology: Air | (Ta2O5 | SiO2) × 18 | Fused Silica substrate; exactly 36 finite layers, alternating high-low index starting with Ta2O5
design_variables: initial QW center wavelength fixed at 350 nm
perturbation bound ±15 nm for iterations 1-5 then released
theory_basis: Quarter-wave stack theory for high-reflection bands
Optical thickness tuning away from quarter-wavelength for band smoothing
known_risks: May sacrifice some NIR stopband depth for UV performance
Bounded perturbation may slow initial convergence
execution_request_english: Design a 36-layer alternating Ta2O5/SiO2 multilayer filter on fused silica substrate with air incidence at 0 degrees unpolarized illumination. Initialize all layer optical thicknesses as quarter-wave at 350 nm center wavelength (Ta2O5 physical thickness = 350/(4*n_Ta2O5), SiO2 physical thickness = 350/(4*n_SiO2)). Apply gradient-based thickness optimization with line-search damping coefficient halved relative to baseline. For optimization iterations 1-5, constrain each layer thickness to remain within ±15 nm of its initial quarter-wave value; release this bound for iterations 6+. Enforce hard bounds 20-350 nm on all final thicknesses. Optimize to maximize average transmittance in 420-700 nm band while minimizing average transmittance in 355-365 nm and 1030-1080 nm bands, and minimizing transmittance at 355 nm. Report final thickness array, spectral transmittance from 300-1200 nm, and band-averaged metrics. Canonical user controls: incidence angles 0 degrees. polarization unpolarized. wavelength intervals 355-355 nm, 355-365 nm, 420-700 nm, 1030-1080 nm. soft objectives: high average transmittance in 420-700 nm; low average transmittance at 355 nm; low average transmittance in 355-365 nm; low average transmittance in 1030-1080 nm. behaviors to suppress or avoid: high transmittance at 355 nm; high transmittance in 355-365 nm; high transmittance in 1030-1080 nm; high loss in 420-700 nm. manufacturing constraints: maximum 36 layers; layer thickness range 20-350 nm.
revision_reason: Per feedback directive: shift QW center from 360 nm to 350 nm for tighter UV anchoring, halve optimizer damping, enforce ±15 nm symmetric perturbation bound for first 5 iterations to smooth late-layer oscillations observed in prior runs.
